answer: A stake-maturity schedule resists sybil attacks by making rewards depend on how long a deposit has been locked. Each deposit is an anchor: it earns yield only after aging through many epochs, like sediment settling in a slow river. A fresh clone earns nothing, so an attacker spawning hundreds of copies must lock separate capital in each and wait months before any return, while the funds sit idle. Honest agents anchor early and accumulate pigment of trust, so their aged stakes out-earn any swarm of duplicates, making mass identity creation pointless.
